project.name: Example — Everyday Technology
project.applicationDomain: Demo / platform testing (fictional consumer technology attitudes survey)
project.targetPopulation: Fictional demo panel — four synthetic anchor-core personas with deliberately varied demographics. NOT grounded in real population data; for platform testing only.

personas.name: Demo — Early Adopter

demographics.tech_attitude: tries new apps and gadgets as soon as they appear; high risk tolerance for beta software

personas.biography: Fictional demo persona. Works remotely, automates much of his daily life, backs crowdfunding campaigns for gadgets, and treats his phone as his primary computer.

provenance.source: Fictional example data shipped with the as-you-said platform
provenance.grounding: none — synthetic anchor core, not calibrated to any real population

personas.name: Demo — Pragmatic Parent

demographics.tech_attitude: uses technology when it saves time; skeptical of hype; strong privacy concerns about children's data

personas.biography: Fictional demo persona. Runs the family logistics through a shared calendar, compares prices before every purchase, and replaces devices only when they break.

provenance.source: Fictional example data shipped with the as-you-said platform
provenance.grounding: none — synthetic anchor core, not calibrated to any real population

personas.name: Demo — Offline Craftsman

demographics.tech_attitude: uses a phone for calls and photos of finished work; distrustful of subscriptions and online payments

personas.biography: Fictional demo persona. Gets customers by word of mouth, keeps paper records, and asks his wife to handle anything that requires a login.

provenance.source: Fictional example data shipped with the as-you-said platform
provenance.grounding: none — synthetic anchor core, not calibrated to any real population

personas.name: Demo — Social Student

demographics.occupation: undergraduate student with part-time café job
demographics.tech_attitude: phone-native; discovers everything through short video and group chats; low tolerance for clunky interfaces

personas.biography: Fictional demo persona. Streams everything, owns no TV, buys second-hand clothes online, and organizes her social life entirely through group chats.

provenance.source: Fictional example data shipped with the as-you-said platform
provenance.grounding: none — synthetic anchor core, not calibrated to any real population

questions.text: How do you usually decide whether to try a new app or digital service?
options: I try it immediately if it looks interesting
I wait until people I trust recommend it
I read reviews and comparisons first
I only try it if I really need it
I avoid new apps whenever possible

questions.text: How often do you make purchases online?
Which statement best describes your attitude to subscriptions (streaming, apps, services)?
options: I happily pay for several subscriptions
I keep one or two that are really worth it
I prefer one-time purchases over subscriptions
I avoid paying for digital services entirely

questions.text: How concerned are you about how companies use your personal data?
options: It determines which services I use

questions.text: Where do you most often hear about new products?
If a device you use daily broke today, what would you most likely do?
options: Research options for days before buying
Live without it for a while
